basis: Predominantly a salivary gland carcinoma; uncommon tracheobronchial origins do not define most cases.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brain malformations define disease; renal TMA is variable, and common renal, cardiac or pulmonary damage is not established.
Recurrent inflammation of subcutaneous fat defines disease; autoimmunity and visceral enlargement occur in only 5-29%; pain and nausea do not establish organ damage.
Defined here as Kunjin viral encephalitis with infection and inflammation of the brain.
Cutaneous angioedema defines the phenotype (4/4); vascular permeability does not establish vessel injury or an immune mechanism.
Meningeal tumor in the anterior cranial fossa; the skull location does not establish bone involvement.
Congenital abnormal connections of the great arteries and associated cardiac malformations; hypoxemia does not establish lung damage.
Disease of the rectum, part of the gastrointestinal tract.
Lens-induced inflammation of the iris and ciliary body involves an immune response to lens material.
Osteopetrosis with hypogammaglobulinemia (IgG low in 3/4); progressive visual loss in 8/8 from optic compression. Organ enlargement alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Isolated impaired spermatogenesis and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Bilateral congenital absence or underdevelopment of the radial skeletal structures.
Brain dysfunction caused by severe hypertension defines this hypertensive neurovascular disorder.
Enteric neuropathy; hypogammaglobulinemia 80-99%; ear canal atresia 6/6 and hearing loss 3/3. Cardiac defects (80-99%) and contractures (3/6) omitted by cap.
Radiation-induced bone necrosis is the disease itself and defines its primary organ.
Benign tumor arising in lung tissue; perivascular differentiation does not establish vascular disease.
Structural aneurysm of an intracranial artery; brain injury from rupture is not intrinsic to every aneurysm.
Degeneration and resorption of the distal phalangeal bones.
Skin, hair, sweat gland and dental defects define disease; ocular surface injury occurs in 30-79%. Asthma is separate; immunodeficiency defines a rare subtype.
Malignant neoplasm involving the parietal lobe of the brain.
Adrenal medullary endocrine tumor; direct catecholamine-induced hypertension occurs in roughly 80-90%, including sustained hypertension in about half.
Herpes simplex infection directly damages the corneal epithelium, producing dendritic ulcers.
Mediastinal smooth-muscle soft-tissue malignancy; no specified origin in lung, vessels or locomotor tissues, and mediastinal soft tissue has no axis.
Skeletal myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy both occur in 5/5 and define the syndrome; ptosis reflects muscle weakness.
Sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency is an inborn metabolic disorder causing motor and sensory axonal neuropathy; weakness is neurogenic.
